# Porting notes

## Scope

The R package exports four computational functions:

- `zrnorm(n)`
- `zrexp(n)`
- `zrunif(n)`
- `zsetseed(s)`

All four are translated.  R `.Call` registration and the demonstration client
R packages are interface examples rather than numerical algorithms and are not
compiled by the Fortran package.  They are retained in `upstream/`.

The public methods of the upstream C++ `Ziggurat` class are also represented by
`type(ziggurat_rng)`: scalar generators, `kiss`, seed access, and four-word
state save/restore.

## Unsigned 32-bit arithmetic

Fortran does not have a portable unsigned 32-bit integer type.  The translation
stores each upstream `uint32_t` word in `integer(int64)` constrained to
0..2^32-1.  Multiplication, shifts, XORs, and additions are explicitly reduced
modulo 2^32.  Values used as upstream `int32_t` are converted explicitly to the
two's-complement signed range.  This avoids depending on signed overflow.

## Exact-stream compatibility

The tests were generated by compiling the supplied `inst/include/zigg/header`
directly as C++ and seeding with 12345.  The Fortran implementation reproduces
the first 20 normal, exponential, and uniform values and the resulting KISS
state.

The exponential table initialization deliberately preserves the upstream line

```cpp
ke[0] = (uint32_t) (de/q)*m2;
```

including its cast precedence.  Since `de/q < 1`, upstream `ke[0]` is zero.
Changing this to the more usual `uint32_t((de/q)*m2)` would change the stream,
so the Fortran port does not "correct" it.

## Default initialization

The C++ class seeds from the current wall-clock milliseconds unless
`ZIGG_USE_ORIGINAL_FIXED_INITIALIZATION` is defined.  The Fortran default
object similarly obtains a `system_clock` value on first use.  Reproducible
work should always call `zsetseed` or `rng%set_seed` explicitly.

## Numerical caveat

The implementation intentionally uses the constants and table formulas from
upstream.  It is not a cryptographic RNG and inherits the period/quality caveats
stated by the original package.
